knowledge_units.context_summary: The study establishes a phenomenological theory for the anomalous Hall effect (AHE) driven by nonlinear magnetoelectric coupling in magnets. It identifies that specific magnetic point groups host AHE induced by uni-axial, bi-axial, or tri-axial electric fields, which is reversible by reversing magnetic orders. First-principles calculations suggest Cr2O3 and CoF2 as candidate materials for this effect.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study uses group-theoretical analysis to establish a phenomenological theory for spontaneous and electric-field-driven anomalous Hall effects in crystalline materials. It identifies that type-I and type-III magnetic point groups support these effects via linear or nonlinear magnetoelectric coupling. First-principles calculations suggest Cr2O3 and CoF2 as candidate materials for electric-field-induced anomalous Hall effects via nonlinear coupling.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The text analyzes how magnetic point groups (MPGs) determine the existence of magnetization and the requirements for electric-field-induced magnetization via symmetry operations. It demonstrates that specific symmetry operations forbid certain magnetization components, which can be broken by uni-axial or bi-axial electric fields to induce the anomalous Hall effect. The analysis covers 122 MPGs, excluding type-II groups due to time-reversal symmetry, and categorizes 90 type-I and type-III groups based on their allowed spontaneous or electric-field-driven Hall conductivities.

knowledge_units.context_summary: First-principles calculations identify Cr2O3 and CoF2 as candidate materials for electric-field driven anomalous Hall effect. Cr2O3 exhibits first-order conductivity responses, while CoF2 exhibits second-order responses. Reversing the magnetic order parameter inverts the sign of the induced Hall conductivity in both materials.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The target text lists a series of academic references cited in the document. These references span journals such as Physica, Physical Review, Nature, and Science Advances. The citations cover topics including magnetoelectric coupling, anomalous Hall effects, and crystallographic group theory.

Magnetic point groups (MPGs) are classified into three distinct types based on their symmetry operations. Type-I MPGs consist solely of spatial operations without time-reversal, while Type-II MPGs include time-reversal as an independent operation. Type-III MPGs feature time-reversal only in combination with spatial operations.
